claims.text: The starting material contains discrete W particles or interconnected W ligaments within a Cu matrix.
The untreated W–Cu composite exhibits phase separation.
The untreated W–Cu composite contains interfacial voids.
A single HIP treatment at approximately 800–900°C, high pressure, and short duration is the proposed intervention.
HIP at a temperature below the melting point of Cu will promote transient liquid-phase sintering of the Cu matrix.
High pressure and the selected temperature will make Cu sufficiently mobile to wet W ligaments.
The HIP treatment will improve atomic diffusion across the W–Cu interface.
Improved wetting and diffusion will enhance W–Cu interfacial bonding.
A transient liquid phase in the Cu matrix will heal interfacial voids.
The relevant phase-separated morphology contains Cu-rich regions that can segregate or coalesce.
Enhanced interfacial bonding will reduce interfacial energy.
Reduced interfacial energy will kinetically hinder phase separation and void coalescence.
Phase separation and interfacial voids degrade the effective thermal conductivity of the untreated W–Cu composite.
HIP treatment will produce a more homogeneous W–Cu microstructure with sealed interfaces.
The HIP-treated composite will have higher effective thermal conductivity than the untreated composite after heat-transfer and irradiation exposure.
The intervention will only be effective within a suitable temperature, pressure, and duration window.
Insufficient pressure will fail to drive adequate interfacial diffusion.
Excessive melting of the Cu matrix may prevent the intervention from working.
The stability of the HIP-induced microstructure under prolonged irradiation and cyclic thermal stress is uncertain.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis invokes a transient liquid phase in the Cu matrix while also specifying operation below the Cu melting point and explicitly avoiding Cu melting. No low-melting additive, eutectic reaction, or other source of a transient liquid is stated to reconcile these assertions.
